title: 10x Rule
author: Grant Cardone
blurb: Grant Cardone argues that most people fail not because they lack talent, but because they badly underestimate what success will take. His fix is the 10X Rule. Set targets ten times bigger than you think you need, then take ten times the action you think is required. Along the way, he sorts behavior into four degrees of action: doing nothing, retreating, normal action, and massive action. Only massive action reliably gets results. Cardone treats success as a duty rather than a luxury, and warns that aiming for average is a quiet way to fail. He urges readers to stop competing and start dominating their field, and to read fear and criticism as signs of progress. The book's tone is relentless and motivational. Its central message is simple: think bigger, do far more, and never stop expanding.

lessons.t: Why Everyone Underestimates What Success Takes
lessons.b: Most goals fail because people miscalculate the time, effort, and energy required, so they plan for far too little.
Aim ten times higher than feels reasonable, because big targets demand new thinking and even missing them leaves you far ahead.
You can take no action, retreat, take normal action, or take massive action, and only massive action consistently creates success.
